posts.author: GamingImperatrix
posts.body:
They will probably work on fixing up Unite first. They've a lot of bugs to crush. But frankly, as a Unity Developer and RPG Maker Developer, Unite can't be fixed in a way that would make it good.
I wanted them to bring RPG Maker to life inside a 'real' game engine. It would have exposed the entirety of the maker to modification by the developer. We could have extended every editor in the game, changed the very database itself, and built all kinds of new never before seen functionality. No more hiding functionality in notes!
We could have done wild and whimsical things, like replaced the combat with a Mortal Kombat style fighting game, turned it into a platformer, or made it isometric; we could have applied new shaders for crazy fog effects, lighting, and bloom. The customizations would have been limitless.
And coding in c# is nothing like working in Javascript, there's intellisence, there's instantly available documentation in tool tips; I was super excited for the prospect of using a strongly typed languge with an RPG Maker for the first time ever, because it makes building and debugging large complicated things so much easier.
Instead they basically used Unity as a virtual machine in which they emulated a buggy, underexposed, difficult-to-tinker with instance of an RPGMaker-like thing with fewer features than MZ. It was a disappointment on so many levels. There are free assets on the Unity store that do RPG mechanics better than Unite does. I suspect they were both stubborn and irrationally scared of losing their IP in an environment where licenses are closely tracked and Unity would have immediately known if a developer stole their code.
In light of how badly it performed, I don't imagine there will be a Unite 2.
It'll be back to the drawing board and we'll get more of the same. RPG Maker Y, X, and Z. They might go up to 62 pixels, as randomly increasing resource resolution has been their thing lately. If they're kind to use, they'll just build in the ability to change asset resolution so you can use stuff from previous games.
I don't think they'll implement AI because they don't really handle monthly licenses with any other product they produce, and a buy-once-use-always AI would cheat them out of being able to sell us large quantities of DLC. If they did include an AI, the price for it would be almost as high as the RPG Maker itself, it would be a DLC, and they would need to train it on a large quantity of their own assets, rather than stolen assets, so it could accurately produce suitable pixel graphics with every hit of the generate button; it would basically take the place of the character creator and its parts.
Honestly it would be nice to see them focus on high content volume rather than anything else, the way they did when they hit their stride with 32 bit graphics. Our latest RTPs have been passable but thin compared to some of the older Makers.
